corpus:
Rourke v. Talbot Freight Co., 188 F.3d 402 (7th Cir. 1999), arose from a highway collision involving a Talbot Freight tractor-trailer. The jury returned a verdict of $340,000 in damages. On the negligence claim, the court applied a 2-year limitations period; on the accompanying breach-of-contract claim arising from the shipping agreement, the court applied a 6-year limitations period. The jury voted 10-2 to find liability. A party seeking rehearing must file within 14 days of judgment.

State v. Denholm, 271 Kan. 88 (2001), concerned a conviction for aggravated burglary under Kan. Stat. Ann. 21-3716. The Kansas Supreme Court held that the trial court's jury instruction on intent was proper. Denholm was sentenced to 7 years of imprisonment.

Yaeger v. Pinegrove School District, 402 U.S. 219 (1971), addressed a due process challenge to a student's suspension without a hearing. The district court had awarded Yaeger $12,500 in damages. The claim was brought under 42 U.S.C. 1983.

Matter of Castellan Trust, 55 N.Y.2d 310 (1982), involved a dispute over trustee compensation before the surrogate's court. The Court of Appeals held that a trustee's commission is calculated on principal actually received or paid out, not on unrealized appreciation.

Briarwood Cooperative v. Halvorsen, 19 Cal. App. 4th 660 (1993), concerned a cooperative's authority to evict a shareholder-tenant for nuisance. The trial court entered judgment for the cooperative and awarded $6,200 in attorney's fees. The jury deliberated and returned a verdict by a vote of 9-3.

People v. Okafor, 33 Cal. 4th 517 (2004), reviewed a conviction for vehicular manslaughter under Cal. Penal Code 192(c). Okafor was sentenced to 6 years in state prison.
